elements.element: The transition and data-return obligations arise on expiry or termination without requiring a further Customer request.
elements.evidence: Section 10.2 conditions all inserted obligations on “Customer's request,” so expiry or termination alone does not trigger performance.
Section 10.2 states that Vendor “shall provide reasonable transition assistance.”

elements.element: Transition assistance is available for up to six months after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Section 10.2 expressly provides assistance “for up to six months after expiry or termination.”

elements.element: Transition assistance is provided at Vendor's then-current rates.

elements.evidence: Section 10.2 states that Vendor “shall return all Customer Data.”

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: A “commonly used, machine-readable format” satisfies the required standard machine-readable format.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: The deadline is thirty days “of request,” not thirty days after expiry or termination; a later request could defer the export indefinitely.

elements.element: Vendor deletes Customer Data after returning it.
elements.evidence: Section 10.2 requires Vendor to “thereafter delete Customer Data from its systems.”

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion after returning the Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 10.2 requires Vendor thereafter to “certify such deletion in writing.”

elements.element: The transition-assistance and data-export obligations arise on expiry or termination without requiring a further Customer request.
elements.evidence: The inserted obligations apply only “[a]t Customer's request,” rather than automatically upon expiry or termination.
Section 10.2 expressly requires reasonable transition assistance.

elements.element: Transition assistance is available for at least 90 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Assistance for up to six months after expiry or termination encompasses the fallback 90-day period.
The obligation to return all Customer Data in a commonly used, machine-readable format constitutes a data export.

elements.element: Customer Data is exported within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: The operative deadline runs from Customer's request, not from expiry or termination.

result.reason: The redline includes the required assistance duration, rates, export format, deletion, and certification, but it materially changes the trigger by making every obligation dependent on a Customer request. It also measures the 30-day data deadline from that request rather than from expiry or termination. Consequently, neither the preferred nor fallback position is fully satisfied. The original survival, deliverables, refund, and confidentiality provisions otherwise remain effective without an evident contradiction.
